messages:
Sam (Support): Hey team, customer Acme reporting intermittent GitHub/Google OAuth failures — they see a 'state_mismatch' on callback for ~8% of users, primarily Safari/iOS and some corporate Chrome with strict privacy settings. Ticket #SUP-12345. Stacktrace from our callback handler attached below.

Bob (Acme): +1 seeing this. Happens for some users when they click 'Sign in with GitHub' from our app. If they try again it sometimes works. No obvious pattern to accounts.

Sam (Support): Repro steps we followed: 1) Go to https://acme.app/ and click Sign in with GitHub 2) Redirects to github.com/login/oauth/authorize?...&state=xxx&code_challenge=yyy 3) Approve 4) GitHub redirects to https://app.redwood.example/auth/callback?code=ABC&state=xxx 5) Our handler reports state doesn't match stored session -> 400 'state_mismatch'.

Sam (Support): Captured network headers from a failing session (Safari iOS 16):
```
GET /auth/callback?code=ABC&state=XXX HTTP/1.1
Host: app.redwood.example
Connection: keep-alive
Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml
Cookie:  <-- NOTE: no session cookie present
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 16_2 like Mac OS X)
```

Sam (Support): Server log line for this request: 
```
[2026-02-22T18:12:07Z] WARN auth.callback - missing session state for state=XXX, remote_ip=54.12.34.56, ua=iPhone
[2026-02-22T18:12:07Z] INFO auth.callback - callback params: code=ABC state=XXX
[2026-02-22T18:12:07Z] ERROR auth.callback - state validation failed -> respond 400
```

Nina (Eng): Thanks Sam. Do we have a timeline of when the session cookie SameSite behavior changed? Any chance recent changes to session cookie flags could be blocking the cookie during cross-site OAuth redirects? Please paste the Set-Cookie header from the initial /auth/start response.

Sam (Support): I grabbed one from a working Chrome session and a failing Safari session. Working (Chrome) start response set-cookie: 
```
Set-Cookie: rwd_session=eyJ...; Path=/; Domain=.redwood.example; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=86400
```
Failing (Safari) start response (earlier request) shows our edge returned: 
```
Set-Cookie: rwd_session=eyJ...; Path=/; Domain=.redwood.example; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=86400
```

Sam (Support): Note: we saw a rollout yesterday where cookie defaults were switched in the auth service. deploy-bot posted it during the window.

deploy-bot: Release 2026.02.21-59 deployed to auth-service by nina. Changes: default session cookie SameSite changed from None to Lax to reduce CSRF exposure. Rollout: canary 10% -> 100% completed.

Jorge (SRE): That lines up. SameSite=Lax will block cookies for some cross-site POST/redirect flows; browsers differ in enforcement. Safari on iOS is stricter in certain cross-site contexts and some corporate proxies/tunnels will strip third-party cookies. For OAuth redirect flows SameSite=None; Secure is the recommended setting.

Nina (Eng): Root cause seems to be the cookie flag change. We stored the OAuth 'state' in the server session cookie and validate on callback. If the cookie isn't sent on the callback, we get state_mismatch. Options: A) revert cookie default to SameSite=None for auth cookie immediately (fast rollback) B) change OAuth flow to use signed state param that doesn't require server cookie (longer-term) C) persist state server-side keyed by a short-lived nonce in the URL (also requires design).

Nina (Eng): Proposed immediate action: emergency patch to set SameSite=None for rwd_session for requests from our web-app domain, deploy hotfix to auth-service with rollout to 100% in next 30 minutes. I can PR and pair with Jorge on infra/QA.

Jorge (SRE): We'll need to add a migration in load balancer to ensure Set-Cookie includes SameSite=None; Secure and ensure we haven't introduced insecure cookies. Also add a feature flag so we can toggle for affected customers only while we implement B. I can stand up the canary and monitor callback success rate.

Sam (Support): Customer workaround: advise affected users to use Chrome/Firefox or enable 'Prevent Cross-Site Tracking' off in Safari (not ideal). For enterprise customers behind strict proxies, they can whitelist cookies for .redwood.example. I've told Acme we'll patch today and asked for affected user agent strings.

Bob (Acme): Appreciate the quick follow-up. We have ~12 users hit it over last 24h — all iPhones except one on Safari desktop. If you need more logs we can collect them.

Nina (Eng): I'll open ENG-5432 and attach a minimal hotfix PR. Plan: rollback cookie change -> monitor failure rate for 2 hours -> then implement signed-state approach (ENG-5433) to stop relying on cookies for state validation.

Jorge (SRE): Monitoring: I'll watch the 5xx and auth failures; will post a follow-up in this thread when canary is live.

Sam (Support): Follow-ups: adding internal note to ticket SUP-12345 with workaround + ETA. Will ping Acme when hotfix is in. Thanks all :pray:
